- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment drops below 0.4.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — particularly when prices are trending upward — and add a small upward bias to compensate.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; model should not overshoot by more than 2–3% relative to recent 7-day average unless sentiment is strongly trending.
- When sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., >0.7 over 3 days), model should lag slightly — forecast should be 1–2 days below true peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid “early peak” bias — do not assume peak occurs within first 7–10 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish and recent price action confirms momentum.
